children: Markets now price roughly a 70% chance of another Fed rate increase, up from about 50% last week.
The Fed is driving the latest move

has recovered toward the mid-158s after briefly falling toward ¥152 earlier this month. The pair’s recent rise reflects the gap between what the Fed may do next and what the BOJ is likely to deliver beyond its latest decision.

Expectations for another Fed hike have climbed sharply as traders focus on persistent inflation, firm US activity and higher energy prices. A move from roughly 50% to around 70% has lifted US yields and improved the dollar’s carry advantage over the yen.

The immediate test is whether US data validate the repricing. Strong inflation, employment or activity figures would keep Treasury yields elevated and support the dollar. Softer data could unwind part of the move, particularly if traders decide the Fed hike is already fully reflected in prices.
The BOJ delivered a hike without enough yen support
by 25 basis points to 1.25%, the highest level in 31 years, but the decision was split 7–2.

Governor Kazuo Ueda offered limited guidance on the timing of future increases. For currency traders, the level of rates is not as important as the expected path. If the BOJ hikes slowly while the Fed remains willing to tighten, the interest-rate gap can continue to favor the dollar.

Japanese officials are also alert to renewed yen weakness. Authorities have conducted rate checks, a step often associated with heightened intervention risk, while Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama has warned that Tokyo is prepared to act.
The chart is bullish, but danger lies ahead
The dollar-yen pair is pressing against resistance around 159.00–159.40. A sustained break above that zone would expose ¥160 area, the latter corresponding to a major Fibonacci retracement.

Initial support sits around ¥157.00, followed by ¥156.55–¥156.65. A break below that zone would weaken the recovery and bring ¥155.30 into focus. Below there, the September low near ¥152.80 becomes the larger downside reference.
Traders should treat any move toward ¥160 as a policy-risk event, not simply a technical breakout. The bullish dollar case is strongest while US rate expectations rise and the BOJ remains cautious.
But a softer US data surprise, a more hawkish Ueda message or another Japanese rate check could produce a fast reversal.

title: USD/JPY: Dollar Powers Up Above ¥158.50 as Traders Lift Rate-Hike Bets to 70%
